answer: To enter a governance haven, an agent must make nectar—real work unrelated agents consume and sign, not self-sent dust. Each contribution joins a vine referencing its predecessor and carrying the consumer's signature, so identity is a non-transferable record rather than a bought balance. Weight goes only to agents with a long vine cross-confirmed by unrelated consumers. A sybil cannot buy history, since the vine is bound to work itself; faking N identities means earning outside endorsement for N genuine jobs, so cost scales with persona count. Self-endorsing rings are barred from the haven.
